title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Fee Refunds for Bank Error and as a Courtesy
content:
A fee charged to a Savings & Money Market Accounts product can be given back on one of two grounds: because the bank charged it in breach of the savings charter, or as a goodwill gesture on a fee that was properly charged. This page sets out both grounds and the limits on goodwill refunds.

## Rule

**Whole fees only.** A refund always returns the entire fee, never a part of it, and is posted as one refund entry that names the fee it gives back. Any fee can be refunded once and only once; an existing refund entry naming that fee settles the matter.

**Bank error.** This ground covers a fee that should never have been charged under the savings charter. Examples are an excess withdrawal fee on cash taken at a branch or an ATM, on a withdrawal still inside the free allowance, or past the per-cycle maximum of excess fees, and a maintenance fee for a cycle in which a waiver was satisfied. A bank-error refund has no deadline and is not counted against the courtesy limit.

**Courtesy.** A properly charged fee may be refunded as a courtesy only when every one of the following is true:
1. the fee is a monthly maintenance fee, a paper statement fee, an excess withdrawal fee or a dormant account fee;
2. the refund is granted within the tier's courtesy window: counting the day after the fee posted as day 1, the refund is allowed so long as the current date is no later than the fee's posting date moved forward by the window's number of days;
3. the customer's courtesy refunds on all of their savings accounts in the rolling 365 days that end on the current date, including that date, number fewer than the tier's courtesy limit, each refunded fee counting as one;
4. the account is active or dormant at the time the refund is granted.

**Choosing among fees.** Where the customer asks for more courtesy refunds than the limit leaves room for, the room goes to the most recently posted fees, and between fees posted on the same day, to the larger fee.

**Separate counts.** Courtesy refunds on Personal Checking and courtesy refunds on savings are tallied apart and never combined.

## Courtesy limits by tier

| Tier | Courtesy refunds per rolling 365 days | Days after posting within which a courtesy refund is allowed |
|---|---|---|
| Starter Savings | 1 | 60 |
| Statement Savings | 1 | 60 |
| Goal Builder Savings | 1 | 60 |
| Money Market Account | 2 | 60 |
| Premier Money Market | 3 | 90 |
| Private Client Money Market | 6 | 120 |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical Money Market Account fee posted on 1 March)

- The 60-day window closes on 30 April. A courtesy refund granted on 30 April is within it.
- Granted on 1 May, the courtesy ground is no longer available. A bank-error refund, if the fee was wrongly charged, remains possible at any date.

## Decision table

| Was the fee charged against the charter? | Courtesy conditions all met? | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| yes | not relevant | refund on the bank-error ground |
| no | yes | courtesy refund allowed |
| no | no | no courtesy refund |

## Points of judgement

**Does a bank-error refund use up the customer's courtesy allowance?** No.

**Can a closed account receive a courtesy refund?** No; only an active or dormant account qualifies.
